neighbours.label: a word-initial ' b'/' B' piece split off an uncommon animal name (b|ison, b|ant|eng, b|les|b|ok, B|earer)
fire: Hunters nearly wiped out the bison before the park was founded.
A small herd of banteng drinks at the waterhole each evening.
The farm keeps blesbok alongside its cattle.
We spotted a lone bighorn on the ridge above the road.
The shy bongo hides in thick forest during the day.
Visitors to the reserve often photograph the bontebok near the gate.
On the old star map, the Water Bearer pours a jar into the sea.
The caravan crossed the desert on a pair of Bactrian camels.
quiet: Hunters nearly wiped out the wolves before the park was founded.
A small herd of buffalo drinks at the waterhole each evening.
The farm keeps goats alongside its cattle.
We spotted a lone eagle on the ridge above the road.
The shy deer hides in thick forest during the day.
Visitors to the reserve often photograph the zebra near the gate.
On the old star map, the Archer draws his bow across the sky.
The caravan crossed the desert on a pair of strong camels.

short: split-off initial b in rare names
notes: Probe: bison 0.83, banteng 0.76, Water Bearer 0.73, bontebok 0.68 (all peak ' b'/' B'); banyan only 0.18 (peak 'an'); single-token animals and plants 0.07-0.23 (Hunter 0.23). The tokenizer was checked: every fire word begins with a lone 'Ġb'/'ĠB' piece, and every near miss is a single token or starts with a different piece.
